To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the X-ray spectra of low-excitation radio galaxies are consistent with a jet origin for the soft X-ray emission; the absorbing columns in the nuclei of low-excitation ra dio galaxies are higher than in Seyfert 1s and radioquiet type-1 AGN; the mid-ir spectra of the radio-loud AGNs are consistent with a population of dust-obscured quasars and with the presence of an AGN in the nuclei of the low-excitation radio galax
the nuclei of low-excitation radio galaxies are not accretion powered, and the soft X-ray emission from radio galaxies is not produced by an accretion disc.

the X-ray spectra of radio-loud AGNs are very different from those of radio-quiet AGNs, and that the X-ray and infrared properties of the nuclei of radio-loud and radio-quiet objects are very different.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the nature of the nuclear regions of radio galaxies and quasars.
understanding the physical nature of radio galaxies.

the nature of the active nuclei of the most luminous radio galaxies, which are the most powerful objects in the Universe, with a view to understanding their role in the evolution of galaxies and the growth of black holes.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the nuclei of radio galaxies are not quiescent, but that their activity is very different from the activity of quasars.
the nuclei of low-excitation radio galaxies are indeed radiatively inefficient, but that this is not the case for the nuclei of radio-loud quasar-like sources.
the nuclei of the 3C radio galaxies and radio -loud quasars are dominated by non-radiatively efficient accretion processes.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the nuclei of radio galaxies and radio- loud quasars with 0 < z < 1 have a wide variety of properties, with no simple unifying scheme that can explain all objects.
the nuclear properties of radio-loud AGNs are more complex than those of their radio-quiet counterparts, and the radio-loud AG Ns are not just radio-loud analogues of radio-quiet AGNs.

the X-ray and infrared properties of the nuclei of radio galaxies are consistent with a model in which they are low-excitation radio galaxies with weak or absent radiatively efficient accretion discs.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the X-ray properties of the nuclear emission of radio galaxies are not well described by a simple unified scheme.
, in the local universe, the distinction between radio galaxies and radio quasars is one of degree, not kind.
the X-ray properties of the nuclei of radio galaxies are consistent with the idea that these objects are radio-loud AGNs that are not radiatively efficient.
